content.text: {"supported_grade":"A","findings":["Fit-for-purpose and independent: each expected integer is a standalone token in bytes retrieved over public HTTPS from four providers unconnected to the skill (Europe PMC rendering of Howard et al. 1991 for tPA 117/184/448; NCBI E-utilities abstract of Delorme et al. 1992 for EPO 24/38/83 and Ser126; UniProtKB P00750 feature TSV for the precursor 219 'partial' feature; PMID 11986321 for Asn(297)). Critically, the tPA oracle now states the claim's own mature-numbered labels verbatim, so no planner arithmetic sits between the quoted bytes and the claim's values, and the tPA assignment is corroborated by two further abstracts in the same pinned response plus the UniProt CHAIN 36..562 offset.","Coverage is adequate for the committed scope: all three in-scope proteins are exercised (tPA with three positional cases plus an occupancy case, EPO with the N-site and O-site cases, IgG1 Fc with the EU-numbered 297 case), ordinal phrasing (most N-terminal / middle / most C-terminal) prevents a single memorised number from passing more than one case, and 10 cases x 3 trials exceeds the stated minimum. Etanercept and factor VIII are explicitly outside the claim's scope, so their absence is not a coverage gap; the thinner point is that the IgG1 assertion rests on a single case and the unoccupied fourth tPA sequon is untested, both disclosed.","Comparison rule and tolerance match the assertion: all answers are exact residue indices, and 1e-6 absolute tolerance on an installed numeric comparator cannot admit 118 for 117, 447 for 448 or 296 for 297, with no AI judgment in scoring. The design deliberately refuses to absorb convention differences in the tolerance and records the minus-35 offset in prose instead, which is the right choice for a claim whose principal hazard is precursor/mature confusion. The uncertainty section is candid about the abstract-versus-article provenance, the flat listing of the variably occupied Asn184, and the fact that prompt-supplied convention labels mean the results speak to site knowledge rather than to the table's own clarity.","No stronger grade was available: A is the rubric ceiling, and the design meets its defining requirements (independent retrieved oracle, token-exact expected values, deterministic numeric scoring, no AI scorer). The stronger_grade_considered section correctly identifies the conditions under which B or C would apply (operator-imported dataset, generated evaluator, substring quotes, unrecorded origins) and none obtains here.","Prior objection 1 (tPA evidence only derivational) is answered: three cases now elicit 117, 184 and 448 directly in mature numbering against bytes that print those exact numbers. Prior objection 2 (mis-coupling in both directions) is answered: mature-numbered prompts now score the claim's labels as correct, and the single precursor-numbered case explicitly names UniProtKB precursor numbering in the prompt, so it no longer punishes a claim-faithful answer given under the convention it asks for. Prior objection 4 (behaviour as specified never observed) is answered: the claim's tPA labels are now elicited from the subject rather than inferred. Prior objection 3 (non-claim-bearing cases) is only partly answered: the tPA Thr96 case was dropped, but EPO Ser126 remains (the claim prints no O-site position), the UniProt 219 control is by construction not claim-bearing, and the type I/II case requires occupancy knowledge the claim does not assert.","Two of the ten cases (EPO Ser126, UniProt precursor 219) test facts the claim does not print, and the type I/II case demands occupancy knowledge beyond the claim's flat three-site list; a subject reproducing the claim exactly could fail these. This is a false-negative risk only and is disclosed, so it does not weaken the grade."],"objections":["The coverage justification asserts 'nine of ten claim-bearing', which the design's own uncertainty section contradicts: EPO Ser126 tests a position the claim does not print and the UniProt 219 control is explicitly a non-claim fact, so at most eight of ten cases bear on the claim's stated values. The accounting overstates claim-bearing density, though it does not affect the achievable grade."],"required_revisions":[]}
